claims.text: An actively learned DeepMD-type MLIP can be trained on ab initio data representing both liquid and solid configurations.
The trained MLIP can replace the standard EAM reference used in TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training on diverse liquid and solid configurations allows the MLIP to represent the energetic landscape more accurately.
The demonstrated DeepMD potential has high energy-prediction accuracy, including for disordered configurations.
More accurate representation of the energetic landscape improves reference-target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap produces a smoother and shorter thermodynamic-integration path.
An MLIP reference will significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to an EAM reference.
The expected reduction in free-energy path mismatch is approximately 50%.
TOR-TILD's EAM references exhibit relatively large integration-path mismatches because they inadequately represent the configurational complexity of the ab initio liquid.
The intervention applies to refractory and complex high-entropy alloys such as Nb-Mo-Ta-based systems.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the alloy melting temperature.
The intervention is likely effective only for high-complexity multicomponent systems near melting.
The intervention may be less effective for simpler alloys with less configurational diversity.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction may depend on alloy composition, training-set quality, and temperature.
Parallel calculations using an EAM reference and an actively learned MLIP reference provide a controlled test of the intervention.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant mismatch reduction of approximately 50% or more together with improved phase-space overlap is defined as the falsifying outcome.
